knowledge_matches.title: Connecting a Workstation to a Network Printer Using MyPrint App
knowledge_matches.excerpt: User cannot connect their workstation or laptop to an office network printer.
steps: Open the MyPrint (or My Print Services) application on the workstation.
Select the option to connect to a printer.
Locate and select the desired printer from the available printer list.
Confirm the connection establishes successfully.
If the printer does not appear or fails to connect, verify network connectivity and printer IP reachability, then escalate to Tier 2 support if necessary.

knowledge_matches.title: Diagnose remote access connection failures
knowledge_matches.excerpt: A remote worker cannot establish a secure connection or the connection drops.
steps: Capture the exact error, device, network, and client version.
Check service status and the user's entitlement.
Verify device time, certificate validity, and multi-factor authentication.
Collect client diagnostics and escalate if the failure persists.

knowledge_matches.title: Unlocking Active Directory Account After Failed Self-Service Password Reset
knowledge_matches.excerpt: User reports being unable to reset their Active Directory password and is unable to log in due to an account block or lockout status.
steps: Verify caller identity using standard security verification questions.
Open identity management console (such as SailPoint) or Active Directory management tools to inspect the target user account.
Review account status to confirm if the account is flagged as blocked or locked out.
Execute the unlock or unblock action on the user account in the identity management tool.
Prompt the user to attempt authentication or initiate the password reset process again to confirm resolution.
If the account remains locked or authentication fails after unblocking, escalate the incident to Tier 2 Identity and Access Management.

transcript.text: Thank you calling service desk, how can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello, I am Madhavi Rao. My monitor has no power and the screen is black. I work in Sales at Pune, and this is delaying my morning tasks.

transcript.speaker: Technician
transcript.text: I am Shreya Banerjee. Is the monitor power indicator lit, and does the workstation itself appear to be running?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The workstation is running, but the monitor indicator is off. The screen is completely black. My workstation reference is WS-DEMO-016.

transcript.speaker: Technician
transcript.text: Thank you, Madhavi. Please check the accessible monitor power connector and the switch on the power strip. Do not open the monitor or touch damaged wiring.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The monitor cable is slightly loose at the power strip, and that socket was switched off.

transcript.speaker: Technician
transcript.text: With the equipment switched off, securely reconnect the intact plug, turn on the approved power socket, and press the monitor power button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The indicator is now on, and I can see the Windows sign-in screen.

transcript.speaker: Technician
transcript.text: Please sign in and confirm that the screen stays on while you open a document.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I opened a document and the display stayed on. I can work normally now.

transcript.speaker: Technician
transcript.text: The checks are successful, so I will resolve the incident. The incident number is INC0000016 and the call reference is CALL-DEMO-0016. You can follow progress in ResolveAI.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Shreya. I have noted the references and confirm that I can continue my work.

In the browser’s Settings, select the option to clear the cache. The incident does not document the exact menu path or other options to select.

If the cache-clearing option is not apparent, or the user needs browser-specific guidance, consult the approved instructions for that browser or escalate to the service desk. The recorded guidance does not establish steps beyond Settings > clear cache.

knowledge_matches.title: Connecting a Workstation to a Network Printer Using MyPrint App
knowledge_matches.excerpt: User cannot connect their workstation or laptop to an office network printer.
steps: Open the MyPrint (or My Print Services) application on the workstation.
Select the option to connect to a printer.
Locate and select the desired printer from the available printer list.
Confirm the connection establishes successfully.
If the printer does not appear or fails to connect, verify network connectivity and printer IP reachability, then escalate to Tier 2 support if necessary.

knowledge_matches.title: Diagnose remote access connection failures
knowledge_matches.excerpt: A remote worker cannot establish a secure connection or the connection drops.
steps: Capture the exact error, device, network, and client version.
Check service status and the user's entitlement.
Verify device time, certificate validity, and multi-factor authentication.
Collect client diagnostics and escalate if the failure persists.

knowledge_matches.title: Triage an enterprise application outage
knowledge_matches.excerpt: Multiple users cannot open or use a business-critical application.
steps: Confirm scope, affected locations, start time, and business impact.
Check service health and recent releases.
Link the ticket to an active incident if one exists.
Escalate with evidence and impact.

knowledge_matches.title: Unlocking Active Directory Account After Failed Self-Service Password Reset
knowledge_matches.excerpt: User reports being unable to reset their Active Directory password and is unable to log in due to an account block or lockout status.
steps: Verify caller identity using standard security verification questions.
Open identity management console (such as SailPoint) or Active Directory management tools to inspect the target user account.
Review account status to confirm if the account is flagged as blocked or locked out.
Execute the unlock or unblock action on the user account in the identity management tool.
Prompt the user to attempt authentication or initiate the password reset process again to confirm resolution.
If the account remains locked or authentication fails after unblocking, escalate the incident to Tier 2 Identity and Access Management.
